title: ‘Journalist status cannot be self-conferred’, Supreme Court says on Delhi anti-CEC protest pleas

ai.summary: The Supreme Court questioned whether self-proclaimed journalists should get the same protection as accredited reporters during hearings on police excesses in Delhi's anti-CEC protests.

facts.claim: The Supreme Court questioned whether individuals who describe themselves as journalists on digital platforms should enjoy the same protections as accredited media professionals
facts.quote: The Supreme Court on Thursday questioned whether individuals who describe themselves as journalists on digital platforms should enjoy the same protections as accredited media professionals, saying the status of a journalist cannot be self-conferred.

facts.claim: The court said the protection available to journalists would depend on the nature of their professional credentials and the circumstances in which they sought such protection
facts.quote: The court said the protection available to journalists would depend on the nature of their professional credentials and the circumstances in which they sought such protection.

facts.claim: The bench observed that a journalist’s status cannot be self-conferred
facts.quote: But we are in the realm of atomised individuals doing journalism. A journalist’s status cannot be self-conferred.

ai.background_note: The Supreme Court is addressing whether self-proclaimed journalists during Delhi's anti-CEC protests should have the same protections as accredited journalists, following allegations of police excesses.
